`rcParams['figure.figsize']` is a configuration parameter in Matplotlib, a popular plotting library in Python. It is used to control the default size of figures created with Matplotlib, affecting all plots generated in a session unless specified otherwise at the individual plot level. The value is a tuple indicating the width and height of the figure in inches.

To demonstrate its usage, consider the following example:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Set default figure size
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 5)  # Width: 10 inches, Height: 5 inches

# Create a sample plot
plt.plot([1, 2, 3, 4], [10, 20, 25, 30])
plt.title('Sample Plot with Custom Figure Size')
plt.xlabel('X-axis')
plt.ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.show()
```

When this code is executed, it produces a line plot with dimensions of 10 inches wide and 5 inches tall, adhering to the specified `figure.figsize`. By setting the `rcParams['figure.figsize']`, all subsequent plots will default to these dimensions unless locally overridden using the `figsize` argument in functions like `plt.figure()` or `plt.subplots()`, as shown in the next example:

```python
# Overriding default figure size locally
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))  # Width and height both 6 inches
ax.plot([1, 2, 3, 4], [10, 20, 25, 30], marker='o')
ax.set_title('Plot With Locally Set Size')
ax.set_xlabel('X-axis')
ax.set_ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.show()
```

In this second plot, the figure size is explicitly set to 6x6 inches, demonstrating how local figure size settings can temporarily override the default set by `rcParams['figure.figsize']`. By adjusting these settings, you can customize the appearance and dimensions of plots to better fit visual preferences or publication standards.
